best_echo_sets.commentary: Offers a 10% unconditional Spectro DMG% boost, a 20% CRIT RATE buff for 15 seconds after inflicting Spectro Frazzle and further 15% Spectro DMG% boost for 15 seconds after attacking an enemy that has 10 Spectro Frazzle Stacks. For characters that have the capability to inflict Spectro Frazzle in their kit the 20% CRIT RATE boost is close to permanent, while the 15% Spectro DMG boost should maintain decent uptime in Spectro Frazzle focused teams. Generally the best in slot set for all DPS characters capable of inflicting Spectro Frazzle.

main_echo_options.echo_commentary: Offers an unconditional 12% Spectro DMG and 12% Heavy Attack DMG boost when active in a resonator's Main Echo Slot, making it a solid choice for Spectro focused resonators who emphasize Heavy Attack damage and are looking to use the 5P Eternal Radiance set bonus.

Offers an unconditional 12% Spectro DMG boost when active in a resonators Main Echo Slot and gains a 100% DMG bonus to its attack against enemies inflicted by Spectro Frazzle. This echo is the go-to choice for most resonators capable of inflicting Spectro Frazzle, who are focusing on damage and are looking to use the 5P Eternal Radiance set bonus.

best_weapons.commentary_details: Zani's Signature weapon is by far her best option, thanks to its massive boosts in her best stats: 48.6% CRIT DMG with high ATK, 50% Spectro Frazzle Amplification, and even 8% DEF Ignore with a simple condition (that can be permanently triggered during any part of Zani's rotation). How much stronger this weapon is compared to other options depends on how many other sources of Frazzle Amplify you have access to. For example, with Phoebe's 100% Frazzle Amplify applied, the value of this weapon is diminished due to dilution, but without it, it becomes far more important.

sections.heading: Summary
paragraphs: Zani is a 5-star Spectro Gauntlets DPS who specializes in dealing high damage during the stance she enters in her Ultimate called "Inferno Mode". Her kit is centered around certain key elements, the most important one being Spectro Frazzle which she passively and instantly converts into "Heliacal Ember" in order to charge her Ultimate Forte points, called "Blaze" which she needs in order to execute her combos to access her damage.

sections.heading: Key Mechanics
paragraphs: As said earlier, Zani's main focus will be to build up Blaze for her to use during her Inferno Mode stance. It stacks up to 150 points, so the goal with Zani will be to reach that threshold. There are a few ways to do this:
Entering Inferno Mode (via her Ultimate, 50 points);
Using her Enhanced Skill "Crisis Response Protocol" (10 points);
Converting Spectro Frazzle into Heliacal Ember (5 points per stack).

Heliacal Ember works as a variant to Spectro Frazzle which stacks up to 60 times, but it does not count as Spectro Frazzle, so it does not benefit from any buffs related to it, and as a matter of fact it does not even count as a Negative Status. The only exception is they serve as a way to activate the Eternal Radiance set effects. However, the damage granted by Heliacal Ember is instantaneous and equivalent to the damage Spectro Frazzle would've normally dealt.

Zani has another Forte Gauge called "Redundant Energy" that allows her to cast an Enhanced Skill when fully replenished, which restores some Blaze. As Zani cannot apply any Spectro Frazzle by herself, it is important to restore some blaze, and give Zani an extra Heliacal Ember to activate Eternal Radiance Echo bonuses as well as a 20% Spectro Frazzle DMG Amplify effect for 14s to further increase her Inferno Mode damage potential, making it especially important to build before using her Ultimate. There are a few ways to do this:
Using her Basic Attacks;
Using her skill "Standard Defense Protocol" and its parry variant "Pinpoint Strike";
Using her Intro Skill.

Zani's Resonance Skill indeed allows her to first do a small hit of damage (Standard Defense Protocol) and then enter a parry stance that she can hold for up to 2 seconds, during which she takes no damage for 1 attack (and 30% reduced DMG in the 2 seconds that follow). If an attack is successfully parried, she will execute Pinpoint Strike for extra damage and Redundant Energy, which is enough to cast her Enhanced Skill after an Intro. To get all 100 Redundant Energy points without a parry, following or preceding an Intro Skill with Standard Defense Protocol into Basic Attack 3 should be all that's needed for quick access to her Enhanced Skill. Once this is achieved, Zani is ready to activate her Ultimate and enter Inferno Mode.

During Inferno Mode, Zani gets a new kit featuring new Basic Attacks, a new parry Skill with a new counter (which also doubles as a Dodge Counter), and she utilizes her other Forte bar to execute all of these actions. She gets 50 Blaze points which she'll consume to execute her combos in Inferno Mode (with the cap extended from 100 to 150 and her Ultimate filling those missing 50 points). All of the damage she can deal during this stance is considered Heavy Attack DMG and Spectro Frazzle DMG simultaneously, so all related buffs apply.

sections.heading: Inferno Mode & How it Works
paragraphs: To get into the details of her Ultimate, once Zani enters Inferno Mode, she gains new Basic Attacks called "Daybreak", "Dawning", and "Nightfall". These are the center of her kit in general. The simplest possible rotation only requires you to perform her Basic Attack string 2 times, which casts each of these skills twice. Simple and effective. Daybreak consumes 10 Blaze, Dawning consumes 20 Blaze and Nightfall consumes up to 40 Blaze, with each Blaze consumed giving an extra multiplier increase to Nightfall specifically (other attacks do not benefit from this). That's 140 Blaze consumed at maximum in total.

However, other options are available. Her Skill allows you to immediately enter a parry stance for up to 2 seconds during which she will take up to 70% reduced damage. Parrying any attack triggers an equivalent to Dawning called "Lightsmash" which consumes 20 Blaze, after which Zani can immediately follow with Nightfall. This combo therefore only costs 60 Blaze. The exact same thing occurs if a Dodge Counter is executed. This can be important to factor in to preserve Blaze for lengthier rotations.

Finally, once Zani has consumed enough Blaze and has 30 left or less (the threshold is indicated on her Forte bar), then she can cast another Ultimate called "The Last Stand" which deals some damage, stops in-game timers and prevents you from switching out during it like any regular Ultimate would. This also ends her rotation as it ends Inferno Mode at the same time.

Once all of this is done, she may cast her Outro. It deals a final burst of damage dependent on the stacks of Heliacal Ember present on enemies, consumes all Heliacal Ember stacks present on targets, and also amplifies the Spectro DMG of all characters except Zani by 20% if they have Heliacal Ember applied, which is a small DMG boost for your Supports.

sections.heading: Meta Position & Conclusion
paragraphs: Zani's position in the meta is... interesting, to say the least. Her and her teammates are fully compatible with Quickswap, and her damage can be taken to a much higher ceiling than her baseline performance. The issues arise when discussing her teammates, and her baseline performance.

Without a doubt, for a character as old as Zani, her ceiling in Quickswap is satisfactory and has withstood the test of time as she is still considered meta-viable when fully optimized. However, this performance is completely dependent on 2 very specific characters: Phoebe and Spectro Rover.

Phoebe is a necessary inclusion to her teams, no matter how you put it. Spectro Rover is not sufficient as a Frazzle applier and a buffer. Phoebe doubles Zani's damage, simply put, and that's not something Rover alone can compensate for. She applies more Frazzle, her buffs are so much better and tailored towards Zani specifically. Zani was simply balanced around Phoebe, a fact that makes Zani's teambuilding restrictive, and her team options have indeed stagnated so badly that they have not changed at all since her release. Without Phoebe, Zani is quite literally worse than any Limited DPS that came out before her.

Zani, Phoebe and Spectro Rover are the prime Spectro Frazzle team, and it hasn't changed since version 2.3, Zani's own release date. The Frazzle application of all of these team members together is high enough that, since none of their buffs expire upon swapping, Zani can utilize her excellent Swap Cancel windows on her Nightfall attacks and preserve some Blaze in order to cast 3 or even 4 Nightfalls per full team rotation. This leads to huge DPS increases if it can be pulled off fast enough via Quickswap.

Without Quickswap, Zani and Phoebe are best used with Shorekeeper, and the performance of that team is... questionable at best. The lowest of any 2.x team, falling behind Carlotta by a noticeable margin. Not to mention, the Energy Regen requirements on that team are huge and near-impossible to meet which makes building the team very difficult, and to rub salt into the wound, that's a full premium team, so it's crazy expensive to pull together.

In conclusion, Zani is in one of the most unfortunate meta positions in Wuthering Waves. Only functional in a single team using Quickswap, for casual players she'll be a struggle to get any noticeable results with, her teams are expensive to get up and running, and they take a lot of effort to pull off. Calling Zani one of the worst current investments you could make in Wuthering Waves, particularly as a new player, is a safe claim to make.

synergies.commentary: Phoebe in her Confession mode is the perfect Zani teammate. Providing 100% DMG Amplification, able to run a supportive set like Moonlit Clouds for extra damage and also being able to fully fill Zani's Blaze bar by applying lots of Spectro Frazzle, no teammate choice Zani has can compare to Phoebe, making her the best Zani team choice by huge amounts.

These two are the other Spectro Frazzle appliers Zani has to try to fill her Blaze bar. While neither compare to Phoebe, having 2 Frazzle appliers in the team they can allow Zani to execute 3 Nightfalls per rotation (with some quickswap if Phoebe + Spectro Rover is used) for extra damage, making Phoebe + Spectro Rover the best Zani team when fully optimized (with Ciaccona as a worse alternative if need be).

All 3 of these characters can Amplify Zani's Heavy Attack DMG via their Outros to buff her damage further. While none of them quite compete with Phoebe's 100% Amplification, Phrolova has a lot of personal damage to her name and Mortefi is F2P-accessible with higher buffing. Iuno is an in-between of the two with extra sustain.

As the best generalist Support, it's no surprise Shorekeeper can slot in any team in the game as she provides high team-wide ATK%, 15% DMG Amplification, CRIT Rate and CRIT DMG buffs making her the best option for Zani teams without quickswap (she also has much higher sustain than Spectro Rover if that's desired!)
